data.long_meaning: Divithya is the Sanskrit name for the goddess of wisdom and learning. She is often depicted as the goddess of knowledge, education, and the arts. Divithya is also revered as the goddess of memory, and is invoked by students to help them remember important information.

historical_references.reference:
Divithya was a celebrated saint of the Srivaishnava tradition in the 13th century. He is known for his works on theology, logic and philosophy. He is also the author of the famous commentary on the 'Tattva Thartham' of Ramanuja.
Context: Srivaishnava tradition, 13th century, Literature and Philosophy

Divithya was also known as 'Thirumangai Azhwar', one of the twelve Azhwars or saints of the Tamil Vaishnavite tradition. He composed 273 hymns in the Tamil language, collectively known as the 'Divya Prabandham'. These hymns have been a source of inspiration and devotion for millions of Vaishnavites over the centuries.
Context: Tamil Vaishnavite tradition, 8th-9th centuries, Literature and Devotion
